metadataReview.note: Kressenbrunn is the medieval name of Groißenbrunn in the south-eastern Marchfeld, Lower Austria. Museum Niederösterreich identifies the village as the place of the decisive battle between Béla IV of Hungary and Ottokar II of Bohemia, and Klima’s monograph situates the 1260 events in the Marchfeld landscape. The point marks the village as a sector reference, not the full battlefield or any camp position. The existing month-precision date (July 1260) is retained; the museum’s day, 12 July, is not added. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred, and the museum’s casualty figure is not adopted.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: OpenStreetMap node 88154682 (place=village, name Groißenbrunn) is at latitude 48.2223664, longitude 16.9046470, rounded to [16.9046,48.2224]. Museum Niederösterreich’s Gedächtnis des Landes identifies Groißenbrunn, first recorded in 1115 as “Chressinprunen”, as the place of the decisive battle between Béla IV and Ottokar II on 12 July 1260. This is a village-sector reference, not the Bohemian main camp struck by the Hungarian attack or a surveyed battlefield centre. It is also not the separate battle memorial beside the L5 road (OpenStreetMap node 2324030046, about 100 m south-east of the village node), whose inscription commemorates the battle at Groissenbrunn between Ottokar II and Béla IV on 12 July 1260. No accuracy radius is claimed.
